# Feature: Widget Gauntlet & Copy-Hygiene Harness

## 1. Feature Goal

**ID**: FEAT-032
**Source Plan**: `.spec-lite/plan_interaction_wave2.md`

Make the interaction layer's quality **mechanically enforced** instead of re-established by hand every time a run goes wrong.

Today the layer's only standing regression suite is `packages/core/tests/interaction/widget-regressions.spec.ts` — nine JSDOM `WidgetPort` fixtures whose action counter wraps `click`, `fill`, and `clear` and lets `type` and `press` through **uncounted**, whose page reads are not counted at all, and whose results are reported only as one aggregate suite pass. It never touches `browser-click.ts`, `driveWithRetry`, viewport geometry, controller ref minting, the tool middleware, or the final model-visible payload. Calling that the gate for FEAT-034's five-layer recovery refactor would certify the inner engine while every layer being refactored stayed unobserved.

Copy hygiene is in the same state one level up. Wave 1's `(code, cause)` failure table (`packages/core/src/fill/types.ts`) proved the invariant that matters — _a hint may only name a move the engine has an engineered path for_ — but it covers **fills only**. Controller actionability errors, registered tool failures, and shared middleware/budget refusals are still inline string literals with no distinctness test, no required-detail test, and no capability test. That is the exact defect class that cost run `20260829T171218Z-do-0ae073f1` 13.9 seconds obeying advice the engine could not honour.

After this feature:

- **Three tiers exist and gate CI.** A fast **protocol** tier (JSDOM drivers) with authoritative action accounting; an **agent real-browser** tier (loopback + real Chrome + wrapped tools through middleware) that exercises the seam the model actually sees; and a **message catalog** tier that proves every model-visible interaction message is registered, distinct, renderable, and capability-backed.
- **The mutating-action counter is authoritative.** `click`, `fill`, `clear`, `type`, `press`, and any scroll action are counted as mutations; `observe` / `evaluate` / `evaluateOn` are counted **separately** as reads, so a silent extra page read — invisible in every other signal — fails a test. A port method that is neither classified is a compile-or-test failure, not a silent zero.
- **Every fixture reports its own result.** Per-fixture outcome, mutations, reads, and (agent tier) top-level tool calls. An aggregate green is no longer sufficient evidence.
- **No fixture passes by freezing a known unsupported failure.** A registry entry may declare a commit, or an _engineered_ refusal whose hint resolves to a real capability. "We cannot do this yet" is not a declarable outcome — which is precisely why virtualized lists and open shadow roots are FEAT-037's problem and are absent here.
- **The gallery grows 9 → 13** with four already-engineered generic patterns: re-mounting search form (agent tier), masked input, split date fields, and shared-calendar range pair.

**The hard constraint on every line of this work** (memory → General, plan §1 and §7): **no website-specific logic.** Each fixture declares the nameable _generic_ pattern it encodes. A site name may appear **only** in a fixture's leading header comment as provenance for why the pattern is worth encoding — and that placement is asserted mechanically, because the gauntlet is the easiest place in this plan to violate the rule.

**Explicitly out of scope.** FEAT-032 changes **no existing stable error code** — no code is added, removed, or renamed, and a frozen code-set snapshot asserts it. It adds no fixture for a pattern the engine cannot already drive. Per plan §9, it **captures** today's legacy `errorCode: null` ledger shape as a passing characterization so the gate can observe it; **FEAT-034 flips that to a prohibition.** FEAT-032 introduces no knowingly-failing CI test.

## 2. Data Model (Granular)

> `.spec-lite/data_model.md` does **not** exist, and plan §4 states plainly that **no relational schema and no Data Modeller pass is needed for this plan**. So there are **no tables, no columns, no migrations, and no foreign keys in this feature** — inventing any would be fiction. The granular shapes below are **contract and registry shapes**: TypeScript descriptors held in test-support registries and one source-side message registry, plus one in-memory per-fixture result record. They are designed here because the plan's §4 gives only the conceptual `GauntletFixture` and `MessageTemplate` concepts.

### Entities & Attributes

**`GauntletFixture`** — one generic adversarial widget pattern. Declared once per fixture; the suite is driven off the registry rather than off hand-written `it()` blocks, which is what makes per-fixture reporting structural instead of a convention.

- `file` (`string`) — fixture file name, relative to its tier's fixture directory. NOT NULL, UNIQUE within a tier registry.
- `tier` (`'protocol' | 'agent-real-browser'`) — which harness executes it. NOT NULL.
- `pattern` (`string`) — the nameable **generic** structural pattern, written as a shape ("a control that rewrites what it is given into its own display format"), never as a site or brand. NOT NULL, UNIQUE across the whole gallery.
- `provenance` (`{ run?: string; site?: string }`) — why the pattern is worth encoding. `site` is the ONLY place a site token is permitted to exist as data, and it is asserted to appear in the fixture file solely inside the leading HTML comment and nowhere in `packages/*/src`.
- `field` (`{ selector: string; role: string; name: string }`) — the control the fill addresses.
- `intent` (`FillIntent`) — the semantic request driven at the fixture. NOT NULL.
- `expected` (`ExpectedOutcome`, discriminated — see below) — NOT NULL.
- `expectedMutations` (`number`) — exact count of mutating port/controller actions. NOT NULL. Pinned, not bounded: turn-burn regressions move this number.
- `expectedReads` (`number`) — exact count of page reads, counted separately per memory ("assert it by counting the operation in a test").
- `expectedToolCalls` (`number | null`) — top-level wrapped-tool invocations; NOT NULL for `agent-real-browser`, `null` for `protocol` (no tool seam there).
- `timeoutMs` (`number`, optional) — per-case override for fixtures with deliberate late-arrival timing.

**`ExpectedOutcome`** — a closed discriminated union. Its whole purpose is to make "passes by freezing a known unsupported failure" **unrepresentable**:

- `{ kind: 'commit'; committed: string; resolution?: FillResolution; driver?: string; editee?: { name: string; role: string }; noteContains?: string }`
- `{ kind: 'engineered-refusal'; errorCode: FillErrorCode; cause: FillCause; detailKeys: readonly string[]; followUp: GauntletFollowUp }`

There is deliberately **no third arm**. `engineered-refusal` is legal only for a refusal that is itself the designed product behaviour (handing back two genuinely ambiguous choices; refusing one end of a jointly-committed range) — and it **requires** `followUp`: a second drive that obeys the refusal's own hint and reaches a commit. A refusal whose advice has no engineered path therefore cannot be declared at all.

**`GauntletFollowUp`** — `{ intent: FillIntent; committed: string }`. The proof that the refusal's hint is honest.

**`MessageTemplate`** — the `(surface, code, cause) → { message, hint, requiredDetails, capability }` shape, generalizing Wave 1's `FailureTemplate` (`packages/core/src/fill/types.ts:124-147`) from fills to the bounded interaction-layer inventory.

- `surface` (`'fill' | 'actionability' | 'success-note' | 'tool' | 'middleware'`) — which seam emits it. NOT NULL. Part of the registry key so two seams may legitimately share a code without sharing wording.
- `code` (`string`) — the **existing** stable error code, verbatim. NOT NULL. No new codes in this feature.
- `cause` (`InteractionFailureCause | string`) — the internal discriminator that selects wording. Never serialized to the model (Wave 1 invariant, preserved).
- `message` (`(details) => string`) — the sentence describing what actually happened.
- `hint` (`(details) => string`) — the one next step.
- `requiredDetails` (`readonly string[]`) — the detail keys the wording refers to. Declared, never inferred.
- `capability` (`string | null`) — the exported engine function **or active tool name** that makes the advice work. `null` only for advice that asks the caller to observe rather than to act.
- `capabilityKind` (`'engine' | 'tool' | null`) — which registry resolves it. New relative to Wave 1, and necessary: `packages/core` cannot see the agent tool catalog, so the resolver differs per kind.

**`FixtureResult`** — the per-fixture record the reporter emits (in-memory, one per case; the durable artifact is the test runner's own per-case output, not a new file):

- `file`, `pattern`, `tier` — identity, copied from the descriptor.
- `outcome` (`'commit' | 'engineered-refusal' | 'failed'`).
- `mutations`, `reads`, `toolCalls` (`number`) — observed, compared against the declared counts.
- `byAction` (`Record<string, number>`) — per-method breakdown, so a count that matches in total but shifted between `type` and `fill` is still legible in the failure message.

### Relationships

- `GauntletFixture` 1:1 fixture HTML file, enforced by a directory census in both directions (no orphan file, no orphan entry).
- `GauntletFixture` 1:1 `FixtureResult` per run.
- `GauntletFixture.expected` (when `engineered-refusal`) N:1 `MessageTemplate` via `(surface: 'fill', code, cause)` — the refusal a fixture declares must be a registered template, so a fixture cannot assert wording the catalog does not own.
- `MessageTemplate.capability` N:1 either a core module export (`capabilityKind: 'engine'`) or an entry in the active tool catalog produced by `yantraToolCatalog(buildYantraWrappedTools(services))` (`capabilityKind: 'tool'`).
- Two registries, one shape, **stated deliberately**: `packages/core` and `e2e` are separate workspace packages and neither exports its test sources, so the protocol registry lives in `packages/core/tests/support/gauntlet.ts` and the agent-tier registry in `e2e/gauntlet/registry.ts`. They are unified by a shared descriptor **contract**, not by an import that would breach the package boundary that `packages/agent/tests/boundaries/imports.spec.ts` exists to protect.

### Indexes & Constraints

- **Unique** `pattern` across both registries — two fixtures encoding the same shape is gallery padding, not coverage.
- **Unique** `file` within a tier; census asserts set-equality with the on-disk fixture directory.
- **Total** `(surface, code, cause)` key in the message registry — a duplicate key is a build/test failure.
- **Distinct rendered text** across the entire message registry (Wave 1's `(c)` invariant, widened from fills to the whole inventory).
- **Frozen code set**: a snapshot of every `code` in the registry, asserted equal to the codes the sources actually emit. FEAT-032 changes none; FEAT-033 adds `ELEMENT_OBSTRUCTED` later by editing that snapshot deliberately.
- **Provenance containment**: a descriptor's `provenance.site`, when present, appears in the fixture file only inside the leading `<!-- -->` block and appears **nowhere** under `packages/*/src`.

## 5. Implementation Tasks

### TASK-001: Make the mutating-action counter authoritative, with reads counted separately

- [ ] **Implementation**: Create `packages/core/tests/support/gauntlet.ts` exporting `countingPort(port: WidgetPort): { port: WidgetPort; counts: PortCounts }` where `PortCounts` is `{ mutations: number; reads: number; byAction: Record<string, number> }`. Drive it from an explicit `PORT_ACTION_KIND` classification table keyed by `WidgetPort` method name: `click`, `fill`, `clear`, `type`, `press` and any scroll action → `'mutation'`; `observe`, `evaluate`, `evaluateOn` → `'read'`; `now` → `'neutral'`. Type the table as `Record<keyof WidgetPort, 'mutation' | 'read' | 'neutral'>` so a method added to the port (FEAT-037's container scroll) is a **compile error** until classified rather than a silent zero. Delete the local `counting()` helper in `widget-regressions.spec.ts` and retarget its three Wave-1 cases at the shared counter, updating their pinned numbers to the now-correct totals (`type` and `press` were previously invisible) and adding the read count each case now asserts.
- [ ] **Unit Tests**: A port driven through one `type` and one `press` reports `mutations: 2` and `reads: 0` — the same drive reports `0` under the deleted helper's classification, which is the regression being closed. `observe` and `evaluateOn` increment `reads` and never `mutations`. `now()` increments neither. `byAction` breaks a total down per method. The three retrofitted fixtures (`portal-overlay-combobox`, `prefix-only-matcher`, `click-to-reveal-calendar`) assert both `mutations` and `reads` exactly.
- [ ] **Documentation Update**: Invoke **Document** update mode for the browser interaction testing strategy (widget gauntlet action accounting).
- **Verify**: `pnpm --filter @yantra/core test -- widget-regressions` passes with the new counts; temporarily removing `'type'` from `PORT_ACTION_KIND` fails typecheck (`pnpm --filter @yantra/core typecheck`), proving no port action can go uncounted.

### TASK-002: Registry-drive the protocol gallery — per-fixture reporting, census, and the supported-outcome rule

- [ ] **Implementation**: In `packages/core/tests/support/gauntlet.ts`, add the `GauntletFixture`, `ExpectedOutcome`, `GauntletFollowUp`, and `FixtureResult` shapes from §2 and the `PROTOCOL_GAUNTLET` registry covering the nine existing fixtures. Rewrite the gallery portion of `widget-regressions.spec.ts` as `it.each(PROTOCOL_GAUNTLET)('$pattern', …)` so **each fixture is its own named, separately reported case**, driving `fillField` through `countingPort` and asserting the declared outcome plus exact `expectedMutations` / `expectedReads`. Implement `runFixture(descriptor)` returning a `FixtureResult` and assert against it, so the failure message names the pattern, the observed counts, and the `byAction` breakdown. Add three census tests: (a) set-equality between `.html` files in `tests/fixtures/widgets/` and registry `file` values in **both** directions; (b) `pattern` uniqueness; (c) provenance containment — for every descriptor with `provenance.site`, that token occurs in the fixture only inside the leading HTML comment, and a repo scan finds it nowhere under `packages/*/src`. Enforce the supported-outcome rule structurally: `expected.kind === 'engineered-refusal'` requires a registered `(surface: 'fill', code, cause)` template **and** a `followUp` that reaches a commit, so an unsupported-capability failure is not a declarable outcome.
- [ ] **Unit Tests**: All nine existing fixtures pass through the registry path with their existing semantics unchanged (`ambiguous-suggestions` is the one `engineered-refusal`, with its `followUp` being the full-label re-issue that already succeeds today). Census fails when a fixture file has no entry; census fails when an entry names a missing file; duplicate `pattern` fails; a descriptor whose `provenance.site` token appears outside the header comment fails; an `engineered-refusal` with no `followUp` fails to type-check.
- [ ] **Documentation Update**: Invoke **Document** update mode for the browser interaction testing strategy (gauntlet fixture registry and the generic-pattern review rule).
- **Verify**: `pnpm --filter @yantra/core test -- widget-regressions` lists nine individually named fixture cases in the reporter output (not one aggregate block); adding an unregistered `.html` to the fixtures directory turns the census red.

### TASK-003: Fixture — masked input

- [ ] **Implementation**: Add `packages/core/tests/fixtures/widgets/masked-input.html`. Generic pattern: **a control that rewrites whatever it is given into its own display format, so the value read back never equals the value sent.** The fixture's `input` handler normalizes digits into a formatted string (grouping/separators added on commit) with no site-specific branch anywhere in the markup or script. Header comment carries the provenance; the body carries no site token. Register it in `PROTOCOL_GAUNTLET` with `expected: { kind: 'commit', resolution: 'reformatted', noteContains: … }` and pinned counts. The engine path already exists — `fill/engine.ts:737` returns `'reformatted'` from `state.reformatted` and `:771` composes the disclosure note — so this task adds coverage, not capability.
- [ ] **Unit Tests**: Filling the masked control returns `ok: true`, `resolution: 'reformatted'`, `requested` preserved verbatim, `committed` equal to the mask's normalized text, and a `note` naming the substitution (per memory: report the outcome, never verify the result against the input when the system offered its own answer). The DOM value equals `committed`. Mutations and reads match the declared counts exactly. A second, semantically-identical request that the mask normalizes to the same string still reports `reformatted` rather than `exact`.
- [ ] **Documentation Update**: Invoke **Document** update mode for the browser interaction gauntlet (masked-input pattern).
- **Verify**: `pnpm --filter @yantra/core test -- widget-regressions` shows the masked-input case passing by name with exact counts; gallery census now expects 10 protocol files.

### TASK-004: Fixture — split date fields

- [ ] **Implementation**: Add `packages/core/tests/fixtures/widgets/split-date-fields.html`. Generic pattern: **one logical range spread across two separate date inputs that the page commits together, so setting one end on its own is discarded and the page is left unchanged.** Two labelled date inputs sharing an observable group; committing one alone reverts it. Register with `expected: { kind: 'engineered-refusal', errorCode: 'WIDGET_RANGE_INCOMPLETE', cause: …, detailKeys: ['field', 'partner', 'requested'], followUp: { intent: { kind: 'date_range', … }, committed: … } }`. This is exactly the shape `fill/engine.ts:532-539` already refuses with a hint naming the partner and the precise re-issue; the `followUp` is what proves that advice has an engineered path, satisfying the plan's rule that no fixture passes by freezing a failure.

The `followUp` `date_range` fill then commits **both** ends, with each input holding its own end. The refusal's `(code, cause)` resolves in the message registry and the refusal's hint text is the registry's, not an inline literal. Mutations and reads pinned for both halves.
- [ ] **Documentation Update**: Invoke **Document** update mode for the browser interaction gauntlet (split-date-fields pattern).

Generic pattern: **two triggers that open one calendar which commits both ends together, so the second end must be chosen inside the container the first end opened rather than by re-opening it.** Register with `expected: { kind: 'commit', driver: 'calendar-grid', … }` for a `date_range` intent, with mutation counts pinned tightly enough that a re-open between the two ends (an extra trigger click) fails the case. ## 6. Cross-Cutting Concerns

- **Auth**: N/A. No credentials, keychain access, or consent surface is touched. The agent-tier harness deliberately mirrors `e2e/agent-browser.spec.ts` but drives **no** secret fill — secret handling is already covered there, and adding a canary to the gauntlet would duplicate coverage while widening the blast radius of a test fixture.
- **Error Handling**: No new stable error code, and no change to any existing one — asserted by the frozen code-set snapshot (TASK-007). Messages move from inline literals into a registry with identical rendered text, so the tool seam and the `tool-calls.jsonl` projection stay byte-compatible. `cause` remains internal and is never serialized. Registry lookups that miss are hard failures (`DanglingHintError` / a total-key type error), never a generic fallback sentence — the fallback is what produced Wave 1's "check details.displayedMonths" bug.
- **Logging**: N/A for new sinks. The gauntlet adds no artifact and no log stream; the per-fixture record is the test runner's own reported case. The catalog change is invisible to Pino because the messages it registers are the same strings already logged.
- **Security**: The no-website-specific-logic rule (memory → General) is enforced _mechanically_ here for the first time — the provenance-containment census in TASK-002 fails the build if a site token leaks out of a fixture header comment into a fixture body or into `packages/*/src`. Every fixture is a local static file; nothing in this feature makes a network request beyond the loopback host.
- **Testing/architecture**: `packages/core` must never import `@yantra/agent` (memory → Project Structure), which is why the message catalog is split across two registries and why capability resolution is `capabilityKind`-dispatched rather than a single lookup. Tests stay in mirrored `tests/` directories; the agent tier lives in the `e2e` workspace package because that is where real-Chrome-plus-wrapped-tools already runs.
- **Performance / diagnostic cost**: Memory requires that diagnostic work be paid for only on the path that needs it, asserted by counting the operation. That is exactly what `expectedReads` is for — this feature is the mechanism that makes the rule enforceable, so every fixture pins reads as tightly as it pins mutations.
